subject: coxph model result does not match to "Bayesian inference with INLA"

messages.author: 88ac498246a7fdff
messages.subject: coxph model result does not match to "Bayesian inference with INLA"
parts:
Dear INLA group,

I am trying to do some survival analyses, so I start to compare the results between R and INLA, and go through the chapter in "Bayesian inference with INLA".

I have a few questions to ask,

1. The result I get now is different to the one in the book for "coxph" model with the exact same codes. So are there any changes to INLA could make such difference?

The result I get is:

library(INLA)
library(survival)

veteran$trt <- as.factor(veteran$trt)
levels(veteran$trt) <- c("standard", "test")
veteran$prior <- as.factor(veteran$prior)
levels(veteran$prior) <- c("No", "Yes")
veteran$time.m <- round(veteran$time / 30, 3)


sinla.vet <- inla.surv(veteran$time.m, veteran$status)
coxinla.vet <- inla(sinla.vet ~ 1 + celltype + trt,
data = veteran,
family = "coxph",
control.hazard = list(hyper = list(prec = list(param = c(0.001, 0.001))))
)
summary(coxinla.vet)

Fixed effects:
                    mean    sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant   mode kld
(Intercept)       -1.486 0.255     -1.992   -1.485     -0.990 -1.485   0
celltypesmallcell  0.870 0.253      0.375    0.871      1.365  0.871   0
celltypeadeno      0.909 0.276      0.368    0.909      1.449  0.909   0
celltypelarge      0.280 0.276     -0.262    0.280      0.822  0.280   0
trttest            0.071 0.189     -0.300    0.071      0.443  0.071   0

Random effects:
  Name    Model
    baseline.hazard RW1 model

Model hyperparameters:
                                mean     sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant  mode
Precision for baseline.hazard 442.98 573.30      17.85   243.24    2034.22 40.40

Marginal log-Likelihood:  -261.02
 is computed
Posterior summaries for the linear predictor and the fitted values are computed
(Posterior marginals needs also 'control.compute=list(return.marginals.predictor=TRUE)')

However,  in the book it is the following, and more close to the result from R

## Fixed effects:
## mean sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant mode kld
## (Intercept) -2.194 0.263 -2.731 -2.187 -1.698 -2.174 0
## celltypesmallcell 1.147 0.260 0.641 1.145 1.663 1.141 0
## celltypeadeno 1.216 0.279 0.664 1.217 1.761 1.220 0
## celltypelarge 0.324 0.280 -0.228 0.325 0.870 0.327 0
## trttest 0.169 0.194 -0.213 0.169 0.550 0.169 0
##
## Random effects:
## Name Model
## baseline.hazard RW1 model
##
## Model hyperparameters:
## mean sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant
## Precision for baseline.hazard 437.30 545.22 17.03 237.95 1977.19
## mode
## Precision for baseline.hazard 37.60
##
## Expected number of effective parameters(stdev): 6.15(1.04)
## Number of equivalent replicates : 52.98
##
## Marginal log-Likelihood: -365.47


2. Is there anyway to turn off the Intercept without sum-to-zero constrain on the baseline hazard?

3. To construct the survival data with inla.surv, what's the correct way to specify the counting process format or delayed entry with "(stop, start]"?
  • inla.surv(start, event, stop) ? OR
  • inla.surv(stop, event, truncation = start)?
Much appreciated if you could provide some advice.

Fred

messages.author: 953deaf1a512b96e
messages.subject: Re: coxph model result does not match to "Bayesian inference with INLA"
parts:
Hi Fred,

Not sure exactly of what has changed with the code from Virgilio's book but you can get the results with the R package INLAjoint (from CRAN), where the intercept is part of the baseline. See the attached code, it seems to match.

You can check this preprint for additional details: arxiv.org/abs/2212.01900

For the counting process, you want to use the second option, where you use truncation to continue the follow-up where it stopped.

Best,
Denis Rustand
he...@r-inla.org
